deep_context:
# 2022-254: technical mechanisms, design reasoning and revision boundaries

These notes distinguish published construction from team-stated intent and original engineering inference. Selected numerical values are reported source data, not independently reproduced measurements. The recommended tests have not been performed. A binder snapshot does not certify every competition version.

## SIDEWAYS: compliant dual four-bar collection

Version: SIDEWAYS. [PDF p10](https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf#page=10) · [PDF p14](https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf#page=14)

**Published construction:** Dual pneumatic four-bars; quarter-inch polycarbonate arms; large front and smaller transfer rollers.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Acquire from either side and yield in collisions.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** Two intake directions reduce the turn needed to collect the next cargo while keeping the shooter in a useful field orientation. The four-bar defines the roller’s approach and stowed position; the arm material supplies lateral compliance that the linkage alone cannot. Different roller diameters and reductions establish surface velocities through the transition. An apparent increase in grip is unhelpful if it arrests the ball between contacts. This architecture should be understood as two collectors feeding one shared storage and shooter system, not as two independent scoring paths.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure acquisition at speed and across approach angles, then verify both directions still transfer correctly after impact.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## SIDEWAYS: serialize two wide inputs and reject wrong-color cargo

Version: SIDEWAYS. [PDF p15](https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf#page=15) · [PDF p21](https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf#page=21) · [PDF p22](https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf#page=22)

**Published construction:** Centering wheels and rollers; beam-break position tracking; color sensing; deliberate opponent-cargo ejection.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Maintain two-cargo ownership and consistent shooter feeding.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** The serializer converts a broad acquisition front into an ordered narrow output under a possession limit. Storing the first accepted ball away from the active intake leaves room for the second; that is a spatial control policy, not merely a conveyor. Color rejection adds an adversarial constraint: an unwanted ball must leave without corrupting the state estimate or helping the opponent more than necessary. A sensor detects contact or color at one location, so software must preserve identity as balls move and occasionally slip. A jam can be a state-estimation failure even when all rollers turn.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Run correct/wrong-color pairs from both sides, interrupt the feed, and verify the estimated inventory against video.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## SIDEWAYS: wrap, surface matching and a moving target

Version: SIDEWAYS. [PDF p16](https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf#page=16) · [PDF p17](https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf#page=17) · [PDF p22](https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf#page=22)

**Published construction:** Nine-inch main wheel, driven back rollers, adjustable hood and ±120° turret.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Long contact and controlled spin for accurate mobile shots.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A long wrap increases the time available to accelerate the cargo and can reduce the impulse required at any single contact. Driving the backing rollers changes both friction loss and the ball’s angular velocity. Surface-speed matching is a kinematic idea; the actual ball may slip or deform, so launch spin must be measured. The turret reduces chassis-heading dependence, while the hood and speed map determine range. None of these removes the need to account for robot velocity and shot timing. The relevant comparison is the repeatability of the exit state under a sequence of shots.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure ball translation and spin with high-speed video, compare first and second shots, and test motion compensation across turret headings.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## SIDEWAYS: react against the truss before reaching traversal

Version: SIDEWAYS. [PDF p18](https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf#page=18) · [PDF p19](https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf#page=19)

**Published construction:** Chain elevator, reaction arm, passive telescoping stinger and retention latches.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Reorient the robot to reach traversal within the envelope.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** This climb is a sequence of changing load paths. The elevator first loads a rung; the reaction arm then changes the robot angle by pushing against the truss; the stinger finally reaches a farther rung. Large internal forces can occur while the robot barely moves because opposing contacts create a short lever arm. A tensile strap can carry a known directional load efficiently, but cannot resist compression or uncontrolled reverse motion. The passive stinger can be light because it need not retract under robot load. Copying only its telescoping tubes would omit the reaction geometry that makes the reach possible.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Instrument reaction loads and verify every intermediate retention state; test misalignment and incomplete hook engagement before increasing speed.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## SIDEWAYS: first swerve and deliberately low mass placement

Version: SIDEWAYS. [PDF p13](https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf#page=13)

**Published construction:** Mk4i L3 modules, added motor-shaft support bearings, low solid bellypan and central battery.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Maneuver around defense and maintain stability.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** The drive choice supports the collector and turret by allowing travel direction to change without the chassis continuously pointing toward the next ball. Lowering mass helps resist wheel unloading during fast transitions, while the chosen ground clearance still has to survive real field debris and cargo. Extra bearing support changes how module loads reach the motor shaft. A reusable design record should retain these integration details because a module family name alone cannot explain collision survival or handling.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Compare stopping and lateral acceleration with representative cargo and bumper loads; inspect motor-shaft support alignment after impacts.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

| Intake | 3-in primary at 2.4:1; 1-in secondary at 1.6:1; pneumatic four-bar | [Source p14](https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf#page=14) |

Ratios preserve source notation; verify driver/driven order, complete geometry and the actual version in CAD before fabrication. Figure records retain PDF page and crop bounds in `data/mechanism_images.jsonl`. Images may include rejected prototypes or whole-robot photographs; their captions preserve that distinction.

deep_context:
# 2022-971: technical mechanisms, design reasoning and revision boundaries

These notes distinguish published construction from team-stated intent and original engineering inference. Selected numerical values are reported source data, not independently reproduced measurements. The recommended tests have not been performed. A binder snapshot does not certify every competition version.

## 971 2022: a deliberate West Coast drive simplicity choice

Version: 971 2022 catapult robot. [PDF p3](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RrrDPh5zAsCcHDBvC_XfE8EIunZshhFn/view?usp=sharing#page=3) · [PDF p5](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RrrDPh5zAsCcHDBvC_XfE8EIunZshhFn/view?usp=sharing#page=5)

**Published construction:** Six Colson-wheel West Coast drive; two dual-Falcon gearboxes; 8:70 gearbox tooth ratio.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Robustness, low maintenance and short-distance acceleration.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A differential drive sacrifices direct sideways motion while reducing the number of independent drive and steering mechanisms. That trade can fit a robot whose turret provides aiming independence and whose collectors support acquisition from opposite sides. Wheel choice affects maintenance and turning losses as well as traction. The team’s post-COVID experience constraint is part of this architecture decision: the most sophisticated available module is not automatically the strongest choice when integration and practice capacity differ. Preserve the resource assumption rather than presenting a universal drivetrain ranking.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure short-cycle path time, turning current and defended maneuverability using the actual collector and turret operating policy.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## 971 2022: center and guide cargo rather than only gripping harder

Version: 971 2022 catapult robot. [PDF p6](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RrrDPh5zAsCcHDBvC_XfE8EIunZshhFn/view?usp=sharing#page=6)

**Published construction:** Flex-wheel prototype became mecanum-centered pickup with compliant chain/arm geometry and extra upper guides.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Use known intake behavior and improve transfer support.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** The pickup must establish both ownership and a useful lateral position for the catapult transfer. Mecanum contact supplies centering while the compliant arm accommodates shape and pressure variation. Additional upper rollers address the transition after the initial capture, where a ball can lose support or arrive at the receiver at an uncontrolled height. The lesson is to diagnose the entire handoff path: improving the first roller’s grip cannot solve a downstream gap that lets cargo escape.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Track the ball center through acquisition and transfer with several inflation states; test off-center pickup at realistic driving speed.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## 971 2022: flippy arms combine retention and release

Version: 971 2022 catapult robot. [PDF p8](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RrrDPh5zAsCcHDBvC_XfE8EIunZshhFn/view?usp=sharing#page=8)

**Published construction:** Spring-loaded paired transfer arms; one-way-bearing action opens them when rollers reverse.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Hold cargo in the catapult, then release it for firing.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** The transfer mechanism serves as a timed constraint on the projectile. It must hold the cargo through turret alignment but stop exerting an unwanted force at release. Coupling reversal to opening reduces an actuator but creates a mechanical timing relationship that software must understand. Spring force and ball compression affect both retention and release delay. If the catapult controller assumes the ball is free before the arms actually clear, a perfectly tracked motor trajectory can still produce a poor shot.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure arm clearance and ball release timing relative to motor command, over cargo pressure and spring-wear variation.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## 971 2022: a controlled catapult instead of a flywheel

Version: 971 2022 catapult robot. [PDF p9](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RrrDPh5zAsCcHDBvC_XfE8EIunZshhFn/view?usp=sharing#page=9) · [PDF p13](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RrrDPh5zAsCcHDBvC_XfE8EIunZshhFn/view?usp=sharing#page=13)

**Published construction:** Light carbon catapult, two Falcons, 7:99 tooth ratio and model-predictive launch control.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Team prototypes favored tolerance to cargo pressure and surface-friction variation.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A motor-driven catapult sets the projectile’s velocity through the motion of a supporting arm rather than relying primarily on slip against a high-speed wheel. That can reduce one source of friction sensitivity while introducing trajectory tracking, release timing and structural stiffness requirements. A lighter arm spends less energy accelerating itself and leaves more actuator authority for the cargo. The controller needs the correct state at release, not merely a final position, because angle and velocity together determine the shot. This is a specific tested alternative, not a claim that catapults universally beat flywheels.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure release angle and velocity across inflation and surface variation, compare with the flywheel prototype under equal conditions, and test mis-timed retention release.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## 971 2022: turret structure must also react climbing loads

Version: 971 2022 catapult robot. [PDF p7](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RrrDPh5zAsCcHDBvC_XfE8EIunZshhFn/view?usp=sharing#page=7) · [PDF p10](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RrrDPh5zAsCcHDBvC_XfE8EIunZshhFn/view?usp=sharing#page=10)

**Published construction:** Turret carries catapult and climber; paired bearing support; climber revisions progress toward a spring-extended high-bar package.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Support firing and hanging loads with compact packaging.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A bearing sized only for smooth aiming may be inadequate once the suspended robot applies an overturning moment through the turret. Two support locations can define a load path for that moment while maintaining axis alignment. Shared structure saves space but couples the climber’s strength requirements to the shooter’s pointing stiffness. The documented objective changed from a mid-rung solution toward higher reach, so do not infer traversal capability from a general “climber” label. Each pictured prototype also needs its own competition-use evidence.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Check bearing and mount loads through firing and hanging, verify output-axis alignment afterward, and establish the dated competed climb configuration.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

# 2022-604 — Quixilver: Octopus Prime

Primary source: https://github.com/frc604/2022-public

Reviewed 2026-10-26. This is a source-bounded technical study. Construction, stated intent, interpretation and unresolved evidence are separate.

Code commit: 2cfd645d19ac09681d201481e8eecd10156b2b9d. Read the original FRC-2022 tree. FRC-2022-NEW is a learning rewrite, not certified event code. File locators: Intake.java, BallPath.java, Launcher.java, Climber.java and Calibration.java under FRC-2022/src/com/_604robotics/robot2022/.

## Published FRC-2022 code · drivetrain

### Published construction or code

Calibration defines a 20.5-inch wheelbase and track width, 3.94-inch wheel diameter, 6.75:1 drive reduction and 12.8:1 steering reduction. These are software configuration values, not independent measurements.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Mechanical selection rationale is not established by the code.

### Engineering interpretation

The swerve and localization must be considered together. A configured maximum speed is not a demonstrated match speed. Wheel calibration affects both the path tracker and the launch-distance estimate, so a copied drive configuration can corrupt scoring even when teleop feels acceptable. Check hardware revision, encoder scales and actual loaded wheel circumference before borrowing constants.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Published FRC-2022 code · intake

### Published construction or code

Intake.java configures distinct Falcon 500 roller and deployment motors, a trapezoidal deployment profile, arm feedforward and a 45A deployment stator limit. Intake, eject, unjam and yeet commands are separate entry points.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The code does not state why this exact mechanical geometry was selected.

### Engineering interpretation

The published interface treats recovery and reverse flow as designed operating modes. That is useful architectural evidence, but it does not establish roller material, width, compression or impact survival. A profiled pivot can reduce abrupt actuation; whether it does so under contact depends on the real mechanism and controller settings. Preserve these unknowns rather than infer a later 604 polycarbonate intake in 2022.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Published FRC-2022 code · transfer

### Published construction or code

BallPath.java separates upper and lower Falcon-driven transport sections and exposes position/velocity control and sensor-based ball handling.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Exact transport geometry and team selection rationale remain unresolved.

### Engineering interpretation

Separately controlled transport can stage a second cargo while releasing the first, but introduces coordination between occupancy sensing, launcher readiness and reverse recovery. Code supports the existence of these interfaces, not an independent throughput result or proof of jam-free behavior. A two-cargo game rewards preserving a reliable staged sequence; extra transport complexity should be justified by actual scoring continuity.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Published FRC-2022 code · scoring

### Published construction or code

Launcher.java configures front and rear Falcon flywheel motors with feedforward and feedback. Readiness checks use a five-sample speed buffer and tolerance; distance-related bounds are treated separately.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The source establishes readiness logic, not a published mechanical reason for wheel geometry.

### Engineering interpretation

Requiring recent samples within tolerance is different from checking one instantaneous RPM. It can reject a momentary speed crossing after spin-up or a previous shot. The trade is delayed release versus launch consistency. The existence of front/rear motors does not establish independent spin control in competition, wheel dimensions, a turret, or exact release angle. Those require geometry and event evidence.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Published FRC-2022 code · endgame

### Published construction or code

Climber.java configures three NEO motors and staged first-rung, lift, handoff, high-rung and traversal transitions. It uses filtered tilt and tilt rate, position/profile completion and an angle-history lockout.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Comments explicitly describe gyro-controlled transitions and an antenna-touch-angle lockout; broader hardware intent is not fully documented here.

### Engineering interpretation

This is a dynamic climb sequence, not a simple winch toggle. A transition may require both operator approval and a suitable swing/position state. That ties compliance, sensor filtering, angular thresholds and operator timing together. A traversal state in released code proves intended capability, not a successful traversal in every match or that all events ran this revision. Exact hook and support geometry remain open.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Original code versus learning rewrite · controls

### Published construction or code

The repository README identifies FRC-2022 as robot code and FRC-2022-NEW as a work-in-progress reimplementation for learning and cleanup. Quikplan-swerve and the offboard quixpf particle filter are separate directories.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The rewrite is explicitly described as preparation and learning.

### Engineering interpretation

Do not read the cleaner NEW tree and retroactively claim every behavior was fielded in 2022. The original tree is the stronger starting point for event-era behavior, though its final commit still lacks per-event installation certification. Pin the repository commit and file path when citing code; preserve the distinction between software configuration, mechanical construction and observed performance.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Evidence limits

- Selected primary publications/code reviewed; exact per-event installation and exhaustive intermediate revisions remain unresolved.
- Four previously blocked source originals (2023 robot photo; 2026 serializer, intake and hopper CAD views) were recovered through normal browser downloads on 2026-10-26 and inspected. Whole-robot source views are not exhaustive mechanism or event-version certification.

# 2023-2056: technical mechanisms, design reasoning and revision boundaries

These notes distinguish published construction from team-stated intent and original engineering inference. Selected numerical values are reported source data, not independently reproduced measurements. The recommended tests have not been performed. A binder snapshot does not certify every competition version.

## OPR 2023: low-backlash articulated arm

Version: 2023 articulated arm. [PDF p9](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/2023_Tech_Binder_OPR2056.pdf#page=9) · [PDF p11](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/2023_Tech_Binder_OPR2056.pdf#page=11) · [PDF p13](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/2023_Tech_Binder_OPR2056.pdf#page=13)

**Published construction:** Two driven joints, dead axles, bronze bushings and gas-shock shoulder counterbalance.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Fast repeatable motion with motor-side position sensing.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** An articulated arm can reach floor, station and grid positions without a tall lift, but the endpoint error combines both joint errors. A small shoulder angle error becomes a larger tip error as the arm extends. Reducing backlash at shafts, gears and chains supports motor-side sensing only if elastic deformation remains acceptable. Gas shocks reduce gravitational torque over part of the motion but produce a changing torque with angle. A bronze bushing can be appropriate for high load and limited rotation, while friction and wear must be included in control tuning.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure tip repeatability approaching the same pose from both directions, under load and after chain wear.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## OPR 2023: piece-specific active contacts

Version: 2023 articulated arm. [PDF p15](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/2023_Tech_Binder_OPR2056.pdf#page=15) · [PDF p16](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/2023_Tech_Binder_OPR2056.pdf#page=16)

**Published construction:** Pneumatic top roller for cubes, synchronized side rollers for cones and piece-specific sensors.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Center and hold both pieces while limiting damage.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** The top roller and side pinch solve different shapes rather than forcing both through one fixed gap. Timing the side mechanism prevents one arm closing first and pushing the cone away. A sensor that reliably detects a cube may not see a cone in the same position, which explains why sensing belongs in the physical design. The control should stop or change the roller command after capture to avoid damaging the soft piece. Compliance reduces impact severity but must not let the frame spread enough to lose the intended contact geometry.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Test skewed cone entry, cube retention during traversal and sensor-triggered transitions with worn or deformed pieces.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## OPR 2023: base mass supports arm motion

Version: 2023 articulated arm. [PDF p5](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/2023_Tech_Binder_OPR2056.pdf#page=5) · [PDF p7](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/2023_Tech_Binder_OPR2056.pdf#page=7)

**Published construction:** Low Mk4i base; rear steel ballast and solid bellypan; rigid tower and dead-axle shoulder support.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Stable traversal and a stiff arm reference.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A lightweight arm does not eliminate its overturning moment. Low ballast and a broad support polygon can permit more aggressive joint motion, while adding driving load and stopping energy. Tower deflection appears as arm error even when both joint encoders are exact. The base, tower and arm should therefore be tested as one structure. The appropriate ballast location depends on the arm’s range and battery placement rather than a generic preference for more robot weight.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure wheel unloading and tool-tip motion during combined driving and arm transitions over cable track and platform edges.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## Selected published parameters

| Drive | Mk4i L2; 15 ft/s | [Source p5](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/2023_Tech_Binder_OPR2056.pdf#page=5) |
| Arm | 2×50-lbf shoulder gas shocks | [Source p9](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/2023_Tech_Binder_OPR2056.pdf#page=9) |
| Shoulder | 133:1 overall; #35 final chain | [Source p11](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/2023_Tech_Binder_OPR2056.pdf#page=11) |
| Elbow | 138:1 overall | [Source p13](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/2023_Tech_Binder_OPR2056.pdf#page=13) |
| Intake | quarter-inch polycarbonate; pneumatic piece-specific contacts | [Source p16](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/2023_Tech_Binder_OPR2056.pdf#page=16) |

deep_context:
# 2023-254: technical mechanisms, design reasoning and revision boundaries

These notes distinguish published construction from team-stated intent and original engineering inference. Selected numerical values are reported source data, not independently reproduced measurements. The recommended tests have not been performed. A binder snapshot does not certify every competition version.

## BREAKDOWN: independent vertical and lateral extension

Version: BREAKDOWN. [PDF p12](https://media.team254.com/2023/10/90bc07c6-2023-Tech-Binder-V6.pdf#page=12) · [PDF p13](https://media.team254.com/2023/10/90bc07c6-2023-Tech-Binder-V6.pdf#page=13)

**Published construction:** Vertical elevator plus 15° inclined three-stage carbon-fiber laterator; PEEK guidance rollers.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Fast reach with low moving mass.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** Separating vertical and outward motion turns scoring poses into two mostly independent coordinates. That can simplify the end-effector geometry and let the chassis remain farther from the grid, but adds another flexible stage and a collision envelope between stages. Low-mass carbon structures reduce inertia; guidance roller preload and tube alignment determine whether they move freely without excessive play. The laterator’s angle contributes vertical motion as it extends, so the control system still needs a coupled pose model. A reported travel time describes one axis, not a complete pickup-to-placement transition.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure coral-equivalent tool-tip error under simultaneous axis motion and chassis acceleration; inspect guidance play and cable drag across the entire stroke.

**Limits:** The PDF required OCR. Page 12 elevator construction was checked visually; other numerical OCR details should be checked in the original before fabrication.

## BREAKDOWN: articulate contacts for cones and cubes

Version: BREAKDOWN. [PDF p8](https://media.team254.com/2023/10/90bc07c6-2023-Tech-Binder-V6.pdf#page=8) · [PDF p15](https://media.team254.com/2023/10/90bc07c6-2023-Tech-Binder-V6.pdf#page=15)

**Published construction:** Articulating roller claw with distinct cube and cone contacts; over-center cone grip.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Serve upright cones and cubes without pursuing every floor orientation.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A cone and a cube present different contact and centering problems. An articulated claw can open enough for a cube while using a different smaller contact to constrain a cone. Over-center geometry can supply retention without continuous high motor force, provided the piece is located in the intended three-point contact. Choosing not to solve sideways floor cones is an explicit scope decision linked to expected high-level supply; it must not become a universal claim that such pickup has no value. A local event or a disrupted supply plan can change that assumption.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Test each intended piece orientation and define a safe fallback for excluded orientations; measure grip after approach collisions.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## BREAKDOWN: rack-deployed cube floor pickup

Version: BREAKDOWN. [PDF p16](https://media.team254.com/2023/10/90bc07c6-2023-Tech-Binder-V6.pdf#page=16)

**Published construction:** Rack-and-pinion polycarbonate extension and a small grippy roller feed the main claw.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Lightweight, robust access to floor cubes.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** Linear extension preserves roller height while changing its distance from the chassis, which is useful when a simple pivot would change the pickup geometry too much. A rack cut directly into the side plate reduces part count but concentrates wear and impact load in that plate. The floor mechanism does not solve every piece task; it supplies a known cube path to the articulating claw. That specialization can be efficient when the human-player and game-piece plan makes it sufficient.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Test cube acquisition near walls and with oblique contact; inspect rack alignment and tooth wear after repeated forced retractions.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## BREAKDOWN: forks change the robot’s balance interface

Version: BREAKDOWN. [PDF p17](https://media.team254.com/2023/10/90bc07c6-2023-Tech-Binder-V6.pdf#page=17)

**Published construction:** Carbon-fiber forks and a sliding carriage react against bumper structure; rope lift.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Lift alongside partners and balance quickly.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** The forks are an alliance interaction mechanism. Their usefulness depends on the partner’s underside, bumper placement and where the combined load settles on the platform. Reacting through bumper wood can counter sag but creates a load path that needs appropriate mounting and repeatability. A mechanism that works under one partner may interfere with another, so compatibility belongs in the selection criteria. This differs fundamentally from a cage or rung climb despite sharing motors, rope and lifting motion.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Test with representative partner geometries, unequal loading and platform tilt; verify the load path through the bumper attachment.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## BREAKDOWN: collision avoidance and compliant station intake

Version: BREAKDOWN. [PDF p20](https://media.team254.com/2023/10/90bc07c6-2023-Tech-Binder-V6.pdf#page=20) · [PDF p21](https://media.team254.com/2023/10/90bc07c6-2023-Tech-Binder-V6.pdf#page=21)

**Published construction:** Intermediate superstructure states, reduced-precision transitions and a compliant laterator intake mode.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Move quickly while avoiding collisions and station impact loads.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A Cartesian-looking mechanism still needs a safe sequence through its intermediate states. Requiring every joint to settle precisely at every waypoint wastes time, while removing all intermediate conditions can create a collision. A compliant acquisition mode trades position stiffness for reduced impact, so its transition back to scoring control must be deliberate. Vision and odometry should supply a confidence-aware pose; the mechanical compliance is a complement to that estimate rather than evidence that accurate sensing is unnecessary.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Start transitions from unexpected interrupted states, test a station impact, and verify that the mechanism returns to a known scoring reference.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## Selected published parameters

| Component | Source parameter | Locator |
|---|---|---|
| Drive | 26×26-in frame; L3; 18 ft/s free | [Source p11](https://media.team254.com/2023/10/90bc07c6-2023-Tech-Binder-V6.pdf#page=11) |
| Elevator | 4.64:1; 24T 5-mm HTD; 41.5-in travel; reported 0.4 s | [Source p12](https://media.team254.com/2023/10/90bc07c6-2023-Tech-Binder-V6.pdf#page=12) |
| Laterator | 3.75:1; 18T 5-mm HTD; 49.875-in travel; reported 0.18 s | [Source p13](https://media.team254.com/2023/10/90bc07c6-2023-Tech-Binder-V6.pdf#page=13) |
| Intake | 3.3:1 deploy; 10T 10DP rack pinion | [Source p16](https://media.team254.com/2023/10/90bc07c6-2023-Tech-Binder-V6.pdf#page=16) |
| Forks | 14.6:1; 1-in rope drum; 6.75-in travel | [Source p17](https://media.team254.com/2023/10/90bc07c6-2023-Tech-Binder-V6.pdf#page=17) |

Ratios preserve source notation; verify driver/driven order, complete geometry and the actual version in CAD before fabrication. Figure records retain PDF page and crop bounds in `data/mechanism_images.jsonl`. Images may include rejected prototypes or whole-robot photographs; their captions preserve that distinction.

deep_context:
# 2023-118: technical mechanisms, design reasoning and revision boundaries

These notes distinguish published construction from team-stated intent and original engineering inference. Selected numerical values are reported source data, not independently reproduced measurements. The recommended tests have not been performed. A binder snapshot does not certify every competition version.

## ECHO: compliant vector pickup and cone centering

Version: ECHO. [PDF p8](https://773cbb55-5509-49bc-8d49-05aa4e1c4c70.filesusr.com/ugd/209e0c_40103d44bfcb4b2b877c4b14bb9d1563.pdf#page=8)

**Published construction:** Sponge/noodle roller, dustpan, powered centering flappers and bent-polycarbonate structure.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** The binder lists construction; detailed comparative selection reasoning is not supplied.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A broad soft contact can accommodate variation in approach and distribute pressure on a deformable piece. The dustpan supplies support underneath, while the flappers create a separate centering action. That is a different mechanism from merely adding compliant wheels to an arm. The soft material’s wear and compression set can alter intake behavior over an event; the structure must remain aligned while yielding to impacts. Because the binder does not give a complete rejected-alternatives account, these are engineering implications rather than a claim about the team’s exact selection process.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure centering success across cone orientations and roller wear, and inspect whether the dustpan or flappers create an escape path.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## ECHO: lightweight telescoping arm and roller end effector

Version: ECHO. [PDF p7](https://773cbb55-5509-49bc-8d49-05aa4e1c4c70.filesusr.com/ugd/209e0c_40103d44bfcb4b2b877c4b14bb9d1563.pdf#page=7) · [PDF p10](https://773cbb55-5509-49bc-8d49-05aa4e1c4c70.filesusr.com/ugd/209e0c_40103d44bfcb4b2b877c4b14bb9d1563.pdf#page=10)

**Published construction:** Sheet-metal pivot structure, carbon telescope, shimmed hex interfaces and light dead-axle end rollers.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Weight and backlash reduction are explicitly documented.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** Reducing distal mass improves both arm acceleration and the chassis stability needed to exploit it. A light telescoping tube still needs sufficient overlap and guidance to resist bending and torsion at full extension. Shimmed interfaces target lost motion, while structure and belt elasticity remain separate error sources. Dead-axle rollers can remove rotating shaft mass and simplify the wheel assembly, but their supports must retain alignment. A recommendation should compare endpoint settling and piece ownership under load rather than claiming a material alone makes the arm fast.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure endpoint deflection at full reach and after reversing both axes; inspect telescoping guidance and roller support wear.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## ECHO: nonparallel balance-fork linkage

Version: ECHO. [PDF p9](https://773cbb55-5509-49bc-8d49-05aa4e1c4c70.filesusr.com/ugd/209e0c_40103d44bfcb4b2b877c4b14bb9d1563.pdf#page=9)

**Published construction:** Carbon-rod forks, nonparallel four-bar lift and over-center deployment with ratchet release.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Lift and tilt relative to a partner and the floor.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A nonparallel four-bar controls orientation as well as translation. That can lift a robot while changing its attitude without another actuator, but the force and mechanical advantage vary through the stroke. Over-center deployment can hold a state mechanically, while the ratchet provides a separate release/retention function. Partner geometry and platform angle determine the contact loads. The design should be retrieved as an alliance-specific balance solution rather than grouped indiscriminately with climbers from other seasons.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Model linkage force through the entire stroke and test with multiple partner undersides and off-axis loading.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## ECHO: preload catapult and vacuum swiper are distinct tactical tools

Version: ECHO. [PDF p11](https://773cbb55-5509-49bc-8d49-05aa4e1c4c70.filesusr.com/ugd/209e0c_40103d44bfcb4b2b877c4b14bb9d1563.pdf#page=11) · [PDF p12](https://773cbb55-5509-49bc-8d49-05aa4e1c4c70.filesusr.com/ugd/209e0c_40103d44bfcb4b2b877c4b14bb9d1563.pdf#page=12)

**Published construction:** Spring-released one-shot cube catapult; dual vacuum cups added in a three-day development period.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Preload launch and opponent loading-zone cube acquisition.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A one-shot mechanism can be mechanically simpler than forcing the main manipulator to execute the same autonomous action, but it spends mass on a narrow use. Its value depends on repeatability and the time it frees for the rest of the routine. Vacuum acquisition relies on seal area, surface condition and resistance to peeling; it is poorly described by a generic grip-force number. The swiper is a dated tactical addition, not proof every earlier robot revision carried it. Keep the development date and task boundary attached to the feature.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Test preload release over the allowed setup variation and vacuum retention under peeling loads and imperfect cube surfaces.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

# 2023-604 — Quixilver: 2023 published robot (name not independently confirmed)

Primary source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-presents-our-2023-robot-and-code-release/447255

Reviewed 2026-10-26. This is a source-bounded technical study. Construction, stated intent, interpretation and unresolved evidence are separate.

## 2023 published robot account · intake

### Published construction or code

A pasta-roller intake grips a cone flange and pinches a cube, constraining cones to tip-in or tip-out. A roller reorienter supplies the additional rotational degree of freedom needed for an upright handoff. Rollers are powered coaxially through the reorienter.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team wanted ground pickup in arbitrary orientations; human-player throwing could shorten travel by an estimated 40% and reduce loading-zone traffic. Coaxial drive protects motors and reduces mass at the intake edge.

### Engineering interpretation

This is an explicit strategy-to-mechanism chain: changing the pickup source reduces travel only if orientation and handoff remain reliable. The 40% is the team’s route estimate, not an independently measured cycle improvement. A broad capture envelope transfers complexity downstream unless the robot can reduce the resulting pose uncertainty. Compare full acquisition-to-scoring cycles, including difficult orientations, rather than pickup speed alone.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## 2023 published robot account · transfer

### Published construction or code

A linear intake slider brings the piece inward and permits frontal compliance. A separate horizontal scoring-arm slider reaches across the intake. A time-of-flight sensor first distinguishes orientation at a fixed location, then locates the piece laterally. The elevator lowers while the intake expels to hand off.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team needed handoff despite variable piece position across the intake width.

### Engineering interpretation

Do not collapse the two sliders into a single motion. The intake reduces some uncertainty, then sensing and the receiving mechanism handle what remains. This avoids requiring perfect passive centering, at the cost of coordinated motion, sensor interpretation and collision clearance. Sensor occlusion, flange shape, cone reflectivity and loaded mechanism deflection are plausible validation concerns, not failures established by this publication.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## 2023 published robot account · scoring

### Published construction or code

A non-parallel four-bar provides scoring reach. An Everybot-style lightweight gripper squeezes the cone tip and pinches a cube. The release describes scoring all levels.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team chose the linkage for low mass and long extension, and judged the high-versus-middle scoring difference sufficient to justify the added capability.

### Engineering interpretation

The linkage choice belongs with the piece acquisition and handoff design. Saving moving mass can reduce the drive and tipping burden, but linkage workspace, joint play and gripper compliance determine the usable placement envelope. A later team using a single-stage elevator should not be read as proof that this four-bar was a failed architecture; the game, interface and required motion differ.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## 2023 published robot account · controls

### Published construction or code

Originally the operator selected scoring locations on a driverstation keyboard and the driver triggered automated scoring. The team later reports the driver becoming faster and more consistent than that sequence, reducing the operator role to piece and level selection.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The control allocation evolved with driver performance.

### Engineering interpretation

Automation should be judged against practiced human operation, including recovery, rather than valued simply because it exists. This is a useful counterexample to treating 604’s later single-driver automation as an unchanging philosophy implemented identically every year. Keep the final software release and its 2024-beta port distinct. Detailed drivetrain specifications and the charge-station balancing mechanism are not established by this reviewed release.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Evidence limits

- Selected primary publications/code reviewed; exact per-event installation and exhaustive intermediate revisions remain unresolved.
- Four previously blocked source originals (2023 robot photo; 2026 serializer, intake and hopper CAD views) were recovered through normal browser downloads on 2026-10-26 and inspected. Whole-robot source views are not exhaustive mechanism or event-version certification.

The reviewed publication does not establish charge-station balance construction or exact drivetrain hardware. FIRST’s carried-forward robot-name field is not treated as authoritative identity for this different-season machine.

# 2024-2056: technical mechanisms, design reasoning and revision boundaries

These notes distinguish published construction from team-stated intent and original engineering inference. Selected numerical values are reported source data, not independently reproduced measurements. The recommended tests have not been performed. ## OPR 2024: chassis and module geometry create the intake path

Version: 2024 pivoting shooter. [PDF p4](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=4) · [PDF p6](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=6) · [PDF p8](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=8)

**Published construction:** Modified front module clearance; under-bumper conveyor; post-Newmarket aluminum side plates and added bracing.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Wide pickup, consistent centering and impact rigidity.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** An under-bumper path consumes the same volume as frame rails and module motors, so module orientation and mounting plates are part of the intake design. Increasing plate rigidity preserves compression but can transmit more collision load elsewhere. The documented event boundary should be retained: the stronger side plates and bracing were a precautionary update rather than necessarily the initial robot. Intake width is useful only if the full path can move off-center notes without trapping them at a module or frame corner.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Test side pickup and corner impacts, then compare roller alignment and chassis squareness before and after the update.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## OPR 2024: pre-compression, differential spin and revised release angle

Version: 2024 pivoting shooter. [PDF p11](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=11) · [PDF p13](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=13) · [PDF p14](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=14)

**Published construction:** Pre-compression contacts, independent left/right drives, low-backlash pivot; flywheels later tipped down 6°.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Consistent feed and greater useful shot range.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A flexible note can enter the same nominal wheel gap in different shapes. Pre-compression aims to control that shape before final acceleration. Independent side speeds then create spin, while mechanically linked upper/lower contacts preserve another aspect of consistency. A six-degree structural change alters the reachable trajectory envelope even if the control software is unchanged. Distinguish output speed, compression and release geometry when diagnosing misses: increasing RPM cannot necessarily compensate for a deformed or inconsistently presented note.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Compare shot distributions before and after the geometric revision with the same notes, recording entry deformation and wheel recovery.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## OPR 2024: pneumatic lift and an explicitly different disable behavior

Version: 2024 pivoting shooter. [PDF p16](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=16)

**Published construction:** Dual pneumatic cylinders and revised double hook; single-acting valve retracts on loss of power.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Fast hanging and compatibility with a partner-loaded chain.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A pneumatic climber stores energy before the lift, reducing the need for a large electric winch during the final action. Available force depends on regulated pressure, piston area and the retracting-side rod area, while repeated actions consume finite stored air. The hook geometry must accommodate a chain already displaced by a partner. The described valve behavior is specific to this plumbing and control configuration; it should not become a generic assumption about all solenoids or an instruction to rely on an untested after-buzzer action.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Test force and timing at the lowest expected pressure, including partner chain displacement and the actual disabled valve state.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## OPR 2024: adapt autonomous to whether a note is actually present

Version: 2024 pivoting shooter. [PDF p20](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=20)

**Published construction:** Game-piece camera, drive-to-point correction, missing-note diversion and velocity-compensated aiming.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Avoid wasting autonomous time on absent or displaced notes.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** An intake with a large acquisition envelope becomes more useful when the path can correct toward the observed note. The controller must decide early enough that a failed attempt does not consume the rest of autonomous. A missing-note branch is a strategy choice tied to contested supply and partner routes, not simply a vision feature. The shot system also depends on current robot velocity and a stable angle reference. Database recommendations should include these feedback assumptions alongside the mechanical pickup.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Displace or remove expected notes and test diversion timing, partner-route safety and the resulting end pose.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

| Pivot | ~107:1 overall | [Source p11](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=11) |

| Climb | two 1.5-in-bore, 10-in-stroke cylinders; reported ~200-lbf combined retraction | [Source p16](https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/OPR24-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf#page=16) |

deep_context:
# 2024-254: technical mechanisms, design reasoning and revision boundaries

These notes distinguish published construction from team-stated intent and original engineering inference. Selected numerical values are reported source data, not independently reproduced measurements. The recommended tests have not been performed. A binder snapshot does not certify every competition version.

## VORTEX: centered under-bumper acquisition

Version: VORTEX. [PDF p11](https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf#page=11)

**Published construction:** Mecanum front contact, kicker rollers and angled powered funneling wheels.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Accept side approaches and center notes without jamming.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A note arriving sideways or off-center should be translated toward the feeder before the shooter demands a repeatable entry state. Mecanum and angled contacts can supply that transverse velocity, but excess lateral force can fold or wedge the note. A stiff bumper and intake mount preserve the intended compression under defense. The correct performance measure includes successful ownership from the edge of the mouth, not only straight-on pickup at the center.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Map pickup across the mouth with deformed notes, oblique approaches and bumper impacts; observe the first region where motion stops.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## VORTEX: annular feed removes the intake-indexing heading constraint

Version: VORTEX. [PDF p12](https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf#page=12) · [PDF p13](https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf#page=13)

**Published construction:** Two-direction annular feeder supplies a turret without returning it to the intake; 720° cable system.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Maintain goal tracking during acquisition and feeding.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** The architectural benefit is not merely a large turret angle. Many turreted designs must rotate to an intake alignment before receiving a note, losing continuous tracking. An annular feed trades that delay for a larger guided path whose friction, seams and direction switching must be managed. Choosing the shorter route can reduce feed time, while a reversal must preserve piece state. The cable system makes the aiming envelope physically usable; without reliable wire guidance, the extra angular range is only a CAD possibility.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Feed at multiple turret headings including through a direction change; test note wear, guide friction and cable-chain operation near both limits.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## VORTEX: revised shooter separates feed and launch contacts

Version: VORTEX. [PDF p14](https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf#page=14)

**Published construction:** Second-revision quad-wheel shooter; staged feed rollers; asymmetrical wheels; sector-gear hood.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Controlled note entry and spin for a flatter useful trajectory.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** The note’s flexible ring makes its entry orientation and deformation important to launch repeatability. A dedicated first stage can establish the approach before the high-speed wheels impart the final velocity and spin. Asymmetric contact can bias spin, but the resulting flight still needs empirical validation over wear and range. Hood backlash is an angular error that becomes more consequential at some distances than others. The revision label matters: a final shooter image must not silently stand in for an earlier competition version.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure entry deformation and shot dispersion with several note conditions; compare hood approaches from both directions and both feed routes.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## VORTEX: amplifier is a second routing destination

Version: VORTEX. [PDF p15](https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf#page=15)

**Published construction:** Roller carriage on an elevator routes notes to amp/trap and accepts human-player feed.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Support multiple scoring and shuttling roles.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** The amplifier is not just a final scoring roller. It adds a branch to the note-routing state machine and a distinct human-player acquisition path. Shared use can justify the mechanism’s mass if those roles are valuable in the alliance plan, but creates more transitions and collision states. Passive trap-reaction wheels supply a structural contact during climbing, tying its geometry to the endgame sequence. The agent should explain those dependencies before recommending the package to a team that only needs one of its functions.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Test every routing transition and interrupted sequence; verify that the trap reaction contact does not dislodge the stored note.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## VORTEX: rapid rope climb establishes trap height

Version: VORTEX. [PDF p16](https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf#page=16)

**Published construction:** Sprung hook arms and a low-mounted rope winch pull the robot to trap height.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Lift quickly while enabling the amplifier to reach the trap.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** The climb’s lift distance is determined by the scorer’s required geometry, not just the minimum suspension score. Gas springs can deploy the hooks while the winch retracts them under load. A rope path needs secure anchors, consistent winding and sufficient clearance as the robot swings. If retention relies on drivetrain or motor braking behavior, that exact power-off state should be validated rather than assumed. The trap sequence must preserve the reaction contact and note orientation throughout the lift.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Test acquisition, lift, trap alignment and disable as one sequence with several chain heights and swing angles.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## Selected published parameters

| Component | Source parameter | Locator |
|---|---|---|
| Base | 27×27-in frame; L3; 18 ft/s | [Source p10](https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf#page=10) |
| Turret | 14:52 then 10:125 tooth pairs; 720° range | [Source p12](https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf#page=12) |
| Feeder | 15:18 then 15:15 belt pairs; two Krakens | [Source p13](https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf#page=13) |
| Shooter | 10°–50° release; 32:18 launch pulleys | [Source p14](https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf#page=14) |
| Amplifier | 17-in travel; reported <1 s | [Source p15](https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf#page=15) |
| Climber | 11:40 then 14:42 gear pairs; reported ~1 s | [Source p16](https://media.team254.com/2024/10/8f2607a0-2024-Tech-Binder.pdf#page=16) |

# 2024-604 — Quixilver: Domotron

Primary source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-presents-our-2024-robot-cad-and-code-release/477799

Reviewed 2026-10-26. This is a source-bounded technical study. Construction, stated intent, interpretation and unresolved evidence are separate.

## 2024 release and May 2025 follow-up · intake

### Published construction or code

Polycarbonate rollers flex under impact; short dead-axle sections avoid a full-width shaft permanently bending. The team reports rollers deflecting more than half their diameter in bad hits. Deployment ties the two sides through chain and a cross shaft inside the frame.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Compliance, weight and packaging drove the split-axle construction. The team explicitly reports axle-mount bolts shearing and deployment chain snapping, unresolved during the season.

### Engineering interpretation

A compliant roller is not the same as a robust entire intake. Moving deformation away from a long shaft can concentrate load in axle bolts or a mechanically coupled deployment system. This matters directly to 1833’s request for something beefy: copy the load path and its known limitations, not merely the visible material. The 2026 independently driven arms are a later response to the chain failure, not a configuration that existed throughout 2024.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## 2024 published CAD versus installed hardware · controls

### Published construction or code

The team says bellypan holes were hand-drilled and omitted from CAD, electronics were suppressed to reduce CAD lag, shooter shafts were actually cut shorter, and a reused climber shaft tensioned surgical tubing absent from CAD.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Some differences were drafting omissions, some deliberate reuse and some effort-versus-benefit decisions.

### Engineering interpretation

A released CAD assembly is a valuable geometry reference but not a perfect as-built record. A long shaft in a rendering is not automatically an intended design feature. Likewise, suppressed electronics do not imply an unplanned electrical layout. Follow the team’s replies when interpreting the release. The existing interview synopsis documents the asymmetric launcher and trap system; this addition focuses on the explicitly published manufacturing and intake corrections.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Evidence limits

- Only source-established configurations and changes are described; intermediate revisions may remain unresolved.
- Selected primary publications/code reviewed; exact per-event installation and exhaustive intermediate revisions remain unresolved.
- Four previously blocked source originals (2023 robot photo; 2026 serializer, intake and hopper CAD views) were recovered through normal browser downloads on 2026-10-26 and inspected. Whole-robot source views are not exhaustive mechanism or event-version certification.

# 2024-5940: technical mechanisms, design reasoning and revision boundaries

These notes distinguish published construction from team-stated intent and original engineering inference. Selected numerical values are reported source data, not independently reproduced measurements. The recommended tests have not been performed. A binder snapshot does not certify every competition version.

## ROTI: under-bumper pickup feeds a movable shooter

Version: ROTI. [PDF p7](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JueptXU9TRB6N2dDGX-fZ-d9fCz3nMKs/view#page=7)

**Published construction:** Full-width intake with pickup rollers and centering wheels.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Center notes before they enter the shooter.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** The collector has to supply a consistent location and shape to a scorer whose height and angle can change. Centering at the floor reduces the uncertainty the moving receiver must handle. A shallow pickup can preserve chassis protection but needs clearance around module and frame structure. Surface speed should capture a note without throwing it past the receiving contact. The effective system includes the handoff state that determines when the elevator may move away.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Test off-center acquisition and interrupted handoff while varying the receiver’s initial height and angle.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## ROTI: one lift creates scoring height and endgame capability

Version: ROTI. [PDF p5](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JueptXU9TRB6N2dDGX-fZ-d9fCz3nMKs/view#page=5) · [PDF p8](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JueptXU9TRB6N2dDGX-fZ-d9fCz3nMKs/view#page=8) · [PDF p9](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JueptXU9TRB6N2dDGX-fZ-d9fCz3nMKs/view#page=9)

**Published construction:** Continuous rope lift with overextending carriage; passive lower hooks retain the chain after initial lift.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Use one shooter for speaker, amp and trap.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** Moving the shooter upward changes its release geometry and can improve defended shot access, while stowing preserves travel routes under the stage. That broad capability costs raised mass and a multi-state handoff. The passive lower hooks are central to the climb: they take over the suspension load so the elevator can extend again for trap scoring. Without that load transfer, the same actuator cannot independently hold the robot and reposition the scorer. This is an architectural sequence rather than an elevator plus an unrelated climber.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Verify passive-hook engagement before re-extension; test full-height stability and stowed route clearance with the actual scorer mass.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## ROTI: counterbalanced pivot and shaped note feed

Version: ROTI. [PDF p10](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JueptXU9TRB6N2dDGX-fZ-d9fCz3nMKs/view#page=10) · [PDF p11](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JueptXU9TRB6N2dDGX-fZ-d9fCz3nMKs/view#page=11)

**Published construction:** Gas-spring counterbalance; output-angle sensing; asymmetric launch speeds; conical/mecanum feeder contacts.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** One shooter serves several release geometries.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A counterbalance reduces gravitational torque but changes the motor’s required effort across the angular range. Sensing the output helps distinguish gearbox motion from actual scorer angle. Conical and mecanum feed contacts can shape and spread the note before launch; their useful effect depends on how the flexible ring deforms. The front roller angle also affects trap delivery, so optimizing only speaker shots may degrade another required mode. A recommendation needs the complete scoring envelope and mode transition tests.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure output-angle hysteresis and shot dispersion in every scoring mode, with both new and damaged notes.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## Selected published parameters

| Component | Source parameter | Locator |
|---|---|---|
| Intake | 1.3:1 pickup; 19.6-ft/s surface; 4.8:1 centering | [Source p7](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JueptXU9TRB6N2dDGX-fZ-d9fCz3nMKs/view#page=7) |
| Lift | 10.37:1; two X60s; 1.5-in spool | [Source p8](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JueptXU9TRB6N2dDGX-fZ-d9fCz3nMKs/view#page=8) |
| Pivot | 114.58:1; two 50-lbf gas springs | [Source p10](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JueptXU9TRB6N2dDGX-fZ-d9fCz3nMKs/view#page=10) |
| Shooter | 4-in wheels; 2:1 upduction source notation | [Source p11](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JueptXU9TRB6N2dDGX-fZ-d9fCz3nMKs/view#page=11) |

Ratios preserve source notation; verify driver/driven order, complete geometry and the actual version in CAD before fabrication. Figure records retain PDF page and crop bounds in `data/mechanism_images.jsonl`. Images may include rejected prototypes or whole-robot photographs; their captions preserve that distinction.

# 2024-3467: technical mechanisms, design reasoning and revision boundaries

These notes distinguish published construction from team-stated intent and original engineering inference. Selected numerical values are reported source data, not independently reproduced measurements. The recommended tests have not been performed. A binder snapshot does not certify every competition version.

## NOCTURNE: passive centering trades motor count for geometry

Version: NOCTURNE at Granite State. [PDF p10](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/ih64E84mBXtAJg7fKLBo7rgi5xM.pdf#page=10) · [Team explanation](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/445350/82) · [Team explanation](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/445350/95)

**Published construction:** Fast under-bumper rollers with passive wedges replacing an active-centering beta design.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Reduce current while retaining useful acquisition.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A passive wedge can convert forward motion into centering without another motor, but requires the right approach velocity, contact friction and space for the note to move laterally. If a note is pinched against the wedge before it is captured, a faster roller can make the jam worse. The source represents the Granite State configuration, and a later team account describes impact failures and difficult repairs. The observed update is therefore part of the technical recommendation: a pickup can satisfy its contact objective while losing event value through poor service access.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Test wide and oblique capture, then time a damaged roller replacement and verify alignment after repair.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## NOCTURNE: reuse a familiar joint and simplify the architecture

Version: NOCTURNE at Granite State. [PDF p3](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/ih64E84mBXtAJg7fKLBo7rgi5xM.pdf#page=3) · [PDF p6](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/ih64E84mBXtAJg7fKLBo7rgi5xM.pdf#page=6) · [PDF p7](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/ih64E84mBXtAJg7fKLBo7rgi5xM.pdf#page=7)

**Published construction:** Single-joint arm, paired planetary drives, chain final reduction and output-angle sensing.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Reuse 2023 experience and preserve time before week 1.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A familiar joint can reduce the number of new mechanical and software problems, which matters when experienced students have graduated. It still needs a force-path and backlash review for its new payload. Multiple chain runs can distribute load but require matched tension so one does not carry nearly everything. A hard-stop shot gives a mechanically referenced fallback when vision or arm control fails, but repeated impact into the stop can change alignment. Schedule feasibility is a legitimate architecture criterion alongside reach and nominal speed.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure output repeatability under reversing load and after repeated hard-stop approaches; test the documented fallback with vision disabled.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## NOCTURNE: stage the note before launch while minimizing distal mass

Version: NOCTURNE at Granite State. [PDF p8](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/ih64E84mBXtAJg7fKLBo7rgi5xM.pdf#page=8) · [PDF p9](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/ih64E84mBXtAJg7fKLBo7rgi5xM.pdf#page=9)

**Published construction:** Eight launch wheels; lightweight staging rollers and low-friction guides integrated with the scorer.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Hold and preaccelerate without another storage mechanism.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A staging section can establish a repeatable note entry and prevent an uncontrolled piece from touching the flywheels prematurely. Using a smaller motor reduces moving mass only if it still supplies enough capture and feed force. The structure must resist both wheel vibration and arm acceleration; a flexible mount changes the launch angle even with correct encoder readings. A grippy stage and low-friction guides serve different purposes: one supplies drive while the other avoids wasting that effort. Test the full transfer at operating speed rather than assuming more grip everywhere is better.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Measure note-entry timing, launch dispersion and structure vibration with new and worn notes while the arm is moving.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

## NOCTURNE: the real field exposed calibration and fallback needs

Version: NOCTURNE at Granite State. [PDF p12](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/ih64E84mBXtAJg7fKLBo7rgi5xM.pdf#page=12) · [PDF p13](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/ih64E84mBXtAJg7fKLBo7rgi5xM.pdf#page=13) · [Team explanation](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/445350/82) · [Team explanation](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/445350/95)

**Published construction:** Pose-based shot map, motion lookahead and automatic intake stop after note detection.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** Aim through brief vision loss and avoid accidental extra possession.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** A consistent pose estimate can still be systematically wrong if the practice target or camera geometry is wrong. Calibrating a lookup table against an inaccurate practice field can make reliable local shots fail at an event. A safe fallback should use a mechanically repeatable pose with a validated close shot, rather than trusting the same mistaken distance model. The fixed under-bumper intake also creates a possession-control requirement because it cannot simply retract away from a second piece. Mechanical geometry and sensor timing must be verified together.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Validate against measured field geometry, remove expected vision input, and test closely spaced notes for unintended second-piece capture.

**Limits:** The binder is a published configuration snapshot, not an independent durability or match-rate test.

# 2024-368: technical mechanisms, design reasoning and revision boundaries

These notes distinguish published construction from team-stated intent and original engineering inference. Selected numerical values are reported source data, not independently reproduced measurements. The recommended tests have not been performed. A binder snapshot does not certify every competition version.

## Team Kika Mana: technical sheet supports construction, not a complete design history

Version: Team Kika Mana 2024. [PDF p1](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/f88CQDlOmk8KBTSeom6DQOruSVt.pdf#page=1)

**Published construction:** Asymmetric 3-inch Colson shooter; side-compression feed; rack hood; elevator-mounted scoring package.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** The sheet attributes spin to shot accuracy; broader selection reasoning is not documented.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** This source is useful for geometry and component identification but should not be promoted to a full engineering binder. Different wheel count or speed across the note can create spin; compression controls the contact state and must remain consistent through the feed. A moving scorer adds position and angle errors that require joint calibration. The exact tolerance, rejected alternatives and event-by-event revision history are not established by one illustrated sheet. The agent should use it to locate a mechanism family and then seek CAD, interviews or team replies before claiming why every dimension was selected.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Validate wheel arrangement and compression in CAD, then test dispersion and elevator deflection across the intended scoring range.

**Limits:** One-page technical sheet only. Complete trade studies, final reductions and season revision history remain unverified.
